---
title: "Data browser"
description: >
  Explore spatial gene expression, cell type proportions, ESV scores and PoPS
  disease scores interactively.
---

Select a dataset and a gene to view the spatial expression of that gene beside
the spatial abundance of every cell type. The tables below list the gene's ESV
score for the whole tissue and for each cell type, and its PoPS score for every
trait.

## Notes

- **Count** is the raw UMI count for that gene, exactly as stored in the dataset
  — no normalization or transformation is applied to the numbers you see. The
  *colour* is mapped on a log scale, because raw counts are steep enough that a
  linear ramp would put most positions in the lightest band and hide the tissue
  structure; the colour bar is labelled at its midpoint so the non-linearity is
  visible.
- **Visium and CosMx datasets are shown at different resolutions.** The Visium
  sets have a few thousand spots each and are shown per spot. The CosMx sets
  hold between 181,000 and 1.55 million cells — far more than a plot this size
  can resolve — so their cells are aggregated onto a spatial grid of roughly
  20,000 bins, and each bin reports the **mean** raw count of the cells falling
  in it. Every cell contributes; nothing is discarded. The panel caption states
  which resolution is in use.
- **Cell type proportion** is the estimated proportion of a cell type at each
  position; the proportions across all cell types sum to one. For the binned
  CosMx datasets, each bin shows the mean proportion of its cells. The maps are
  drawn on one common scale so that cell types can be compared with each other.
- **ESV** is the expression-based spatial variability score for the gene within
  each cell type, as reported by `spacelink()` and `spacelink_ctSVG()`; `whole`
  is the score across the whole tissue. A few gene and cell type combinations
  have no score and are shown as not available.
- **PoPS** scores come from the Polygenic Priority Score tables and are defined
  per gene and per trait; they do not depend on the dataset or the cell type.
  Traits are listed strongest first. Genes absent from the PoPS tables are
  reported as such.
- Spatial plots are drawn with an equal aspect ratio. Visium sections use the
  stored coordinates as they are; CosMx sections are mirrored vertically,
  because that platform records its y axis in the opposite direction.
